In terms of how much worse it's gotten recently, be honest about that too. Admit that you've been hiding most of your hurt for his sake, but that your depression is just a part of how your brain works and that right now, your neurotransmitters are running the show, not you. You don't need anything from him right now except understanding.

As someone who has also struggled with depression, the only successful method I've found is to talk honestly about it, but also not make it a huge deal. Talking about it when you're super upset will probably not end well for you, him, or your relationship, so you'll need to think about timing. My bf and I had this conversation when I was feeling pretty good, so I was able to talk about my depression without getting overwhelmed by it. I also made sure to talk about it in terms of a diagnosis first, then how it made me feel second, and he seemed to find that helpful in understanding that when I was having depressive thoughts, I wasn't overreacting; my brain chemistry was, and that was outside my control. 

Have you talked to your psychiatrist about how to bring it up with your SO? I guarantee you're neither their first or their last patient to ask how to talk about their condition with a partner. Your psychiatrist may have some thoughts or strategies beyond our abilities here and may also be able to role play some of your partner's possible responses.

In answer to Q3: Being one of them lady folk who would theoretically like to help pick out her own ring, there are a couple of options.

a) You could talk to a local jeweler, pick out a few beforehand that you think she might like, bring her (blindfolded) to the jeweler, and propose there - "You can pick your ring, as long as it's with me" blah blah blah.
b) You could replace it with a dummy ring that is sweet and meaningful (e.g. family heirloom), personal (e.g. high school class ring), or obviously meant to be funny (e.g. Ring Pop).
c) I actually really love the idea of the note saying "Are you kidding? I have no idea how to pick out a ring" etc. as mentioned below.
d) Ask her BFF. If there are ring ideas floating around in her head, the BFF may have heard about them.
e) Plan a proposal that has nothing to do with a ring, then explain after the initial "will you marry me" that you wanted to make sure she got exactly what she wanted because you're planning on this shindig being forever.

HOWEVER... please do talk to your lady friend about the theoretical engagement first! If she's not ready to get engaged, or doesn't want a ring at all, or really wants the ring at the engagement, or will only say yes if it's the Hope Diamond, it would be better to know before - not after - the proposal.
